Scene: the employee time-card area beside the entrance of a small working warehouse, viewed straight on at standing eye level. Ordinary durable mid-century industrial fittings still in daily use, maintained but rubbed and scuffed. Cream painted concrete block wall with a rust waist-high protective stripe, scuffed concrete floor. A large mechanical punch clock is wall-mounted just LEFT of center, its small circular clock dial blank except tick marks and hands. It has a metal slot for inserting a card and a heavy worn housing. Directly right of it is a clearly separate steel rack of old time-card pockets holding several blank cream paper cards, some edges bent. Far right is a partly open sturdy warehouse access door with dark wired-glass upper panel, metal push plate and glimpses of ceiling trusses through the opening. Narrow cork notice board near far left, almost empty, with one blank paper pinned to it. Main punch clock and time-card rack should dominate the central image and each read as a clear clickable object. Quiet practical space; no people, no hands.
Composition: wall starts at top; primary clock roughly x25-47 percent,y22-63 percent; card pockets x50-69 percent,y22-67 percent; warehouse access door x77-96 percent,y16-80 percent. Floor visible lower quarter. Straight believable perspective, no fisheye.
Wear is specific and modest: polished metal touch points, rubbed door paint, a few plugged drill holes, a repaired plaster patch, darker floor seams. Not an abandoned ruin, not a pristine showroom. No text, letters, numbers, logos, symbols, UI, labels, furniture clutter or cargo. Preserve the reference's flat ink palette and confident geometric clarity.
